punchline: Warren Harding became president in large part because he looked like one.
thirty_sec: Around 1899, political operator Harry Daugherty met Warren Harding and thought: this man looks like a president. Harding was tall, handsome and deep-voiced, but not especially capable. He rose all the way to the White House in 1920 and is widely ranked among the worst presidents. Malcolm Gladwell calls this the Warren Harding Error: a snap judgment triggered by irrelevant cues instead of real ability.
question: When has someone who 'looked the part' fooled you?
